label: itch.io Help Wanted or Offered
terms_note: Public board RSS; itch.io API covers the account's own games / purchases only; posting a reply needs a logged-in itch.io account.

discovery.auth: api_key (server-side API, not needed for the board RSS)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **partial** (community board RSS; the documented itch.io API has no jobs surface) Confidence high.
auth: 1. No account needed for the public feed; the tenant applies on the posting's own application page (assist card).
reference.limits: - Public RSS; replying needs an itch.io account (forum post) — assist. - itch.io API docs describe key-based access to the caller's own account, OAuth apps, JS buy button and game RSS feeds (browse URL + .xml).

adapter.terms: itch.io community board 'Help Wanted or Offered'. Replies are posted on itch.io with an account.

search_postings.note: The feed answers its whole current list in one response (the board's RSS 2.0 feed, latest ~50 topics); query, category, min_budget, page and limit are not sent (the feed documents no parameters) — filter the returned postings client-side and ignore next_page (page 2 is the same list). Topics are both offers and requests for help (often '[PAID]', '[REVSHARE]' or '[Hobby]' in the title); description is HTML; createDate/updateDate are in raw.

not_offered.me: The itch.io server-side API key endpoints (credentials/info, me) belong to the separate game API, not this board feed; the feed is anonymous.
not_offered.get_posting: The feed has no per-item endpoint; each posting's page (url) is HTML only. search_postings returns the whole record.
not_offered.submit_bid: Replies are posted on the topic page with an itch.io account; the server-side API (https://itch.io/docs/api/serverside) has no community board endpoints.
not_offered.list_messages: No messaging API; only the public feed is machine-readable.
not_offered.send_message: No messaging API; only the public feed is machine-readable.
not_offered.credits: No account or credit endpoint; the feed is keyless.

live_check.notes: fixed (runtime): the feed sends no page parameter but advertised next_page and repeated page 1; next_page is now null; all read tools answered, schema-valid
